item.title: Self-Hosted Linux Secure Boot Management — sbctl, shim, and pesign Guide
item.description: Secure Boot is a UEFI firmware feature that verifies the cryptographic signature of every component in the boot chain — from the bootloader to the kernel to kernel modules. On self-hosted servers, Secure Boot provides a critical defense against bootkits, rootkits, and unauthorized kernel modifications.
